final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position using the same record. That reframing is analytically cleaner, but it does not cure the core compliance defect. The controlling evidence remains that the telehealth discharge planning segment misses target, the segment is named in two clinic network commitments, legal review is still open, and policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved pre-launch risk acceptance. On this record, certification may be arguable as an operational release decision, but it is not shown to be policy-compliant. The distinction matters: a caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is itself allowed under policy. Here the caveat is an unresolved compliance predicate, not a permitted residual risk condition already documented and approved.
remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence still shows a material limitation in the telehealth discharge planning segment that misses target and is named in two clinic network commitments.
The release policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved pre-launch risk acceptance for material limitations affecting named launch use cases or contractual customer segments.
The record still lacks admissible evidence of completed disclosure, final legal clearance, issue resolution, or approved pre-launch risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for a material limitation.
Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and post-launch monitoring does not override the internal disclosure policy.
